A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VisAH-FM research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original Muddy Mix experiments, component ablations, trajectory analyses, qualitative results and a human preference study.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and reports a revised preference study and an additional analysis of errors by acoustic source.

M1.justification: The CFM formulation, rollout loss, CLIP–CLAP adapter, timestep conditioning and pretrained VisAH initialization remain unchanged. The expanded description of the inherited spectrogram/waveform backbone documents existing architecture without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use Muddy Mix, including fixed and on-the-fly remixing, and MovieGen examples in subjective evaluation. v3 identifies CMD as the source of existing movie clips; its source-specific analysis partitions retained test coverage.

E2.justification: The comparison methods in Tables 1–12 are unchanged. However, revised Figure 6 adds the unprocessed Input reference alongside VisAH, VisAH-FM and ground truth; v1's corresponding qualitative figure displays only the model outputs and ground truth.

E3.justification: The listening study changes from five participants evaluating eight videos to nine evaluating seven. v3 also reports 44.1 kHz instead of 44 kHz and introduces source-pair aggregation for Table 13. These disclosures do not establish that the retained benchmark experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix G and Table 13 add an error analysis across six boosted/attenuated source combinations. Figures 6–7 provide new attenuation and progressive-remixing examples. Existing ablations remain; v1's PCA trajectory analysis in Figure 4c is retained as v3 Figure 8.

E5.justification: Uncertainty-reporting practices remain unchanged, including the retained trajectory distribution plots. Neither version reports training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. The changed participant count concerns evaluation sampling.

E6.justification: Tables 1–12 retain identical numerical results. Under changed listening-study sampling, VisAH-FM/VisAH/draw rates change from 60/10/30% to 49.20/17.50/33.30%. New Table 13 reports magnitude errors including 0.14 for boosted music with attenuated speech and 0.04 for boosted speech with attenuated SFX. New qualitative examples supplement these results.

T1.justification: The flow definitions, objectives, adapter equations and discrete-curvature definition remain mathematically equivalent. The loudness-difference formula moves inline, and equations are renumbered. No theorem, proof or substantive derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims: generative acoustic highlighting, rollout-based trajectory stabilization, early audiovisual fusion and improved performance over discriminative VisAH.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new source-specific errors through acoustic masking, identifying recovery of speech under loud music as particularly difficult. It also adds a rationale connecting CLAP's text alignment to integration with CLIP. Existing computational, representation and paired-data limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix F newly specifies CMD provenance, the 15,078/1,927/1,789 train/validation/test counts and the source-level corruption procedure. v3 also clarifies the inherited backbone and adds instructions for locating demo.html in a supplementary ZIP. These are documentation additions, not demonstrated changes to dataset splits.

R1.justification: v3 removes Albergo et al.'s Stochastic Interpolants citation and replaces Rouard et al.'s Hybrid Transformers for Music Source Separation with Défossez's Hybrid Spectrogram and Waveform Source Separation for backbone attribution. The broader related-work discussion and research positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main narrative order are retained. v3 simplifies subsection hierarchy, uses lettered appendices, relocates the PCA discussion, adds dedicated appendix sections and makes localized explanatory and wording edits.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from two-column to single-column layout, with substantial figure and table repositioning. Figure 1 is expanded, Figure 6 is replaced with waveform/spectrogram comparisons, Figure 7 and Table 13 are added, and Figure 4c becomes appendix Figure 8.

improvement.justification: The new source-specific analysis identifies a concrete failure condition, while the dataset and backbone disclosures improve interpretability and reproducibility documentation. Revised qualitative figures clarify attenuation behavior. These are useful but limited gains: the method and main numerical evidence remain unchanged, and the listening study has more participants but fewer clips, without added uncertainty estimates.
